name: Veggie egg cups
summary: Eggs baked in little cups over softened pepper, baby marrow, spinach and cherry tomatoes with a sprinkle of cheddar, made ahead for the school-run week.
about: Baked egg cups are a make-ahead breakfast: a tray baked on Sunday covers the first school mornings of the week, and each one reheats in under a minute or travels cold.

ingredients.name: Olive oil
ingredients.note: 1 tsp for the tin, 2 tsp for the vegetables

steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C if your oven is a fan oven). Brush the 12 holes of a muffin tin with 1 tsp of the oil, right up the sides; a silicone tray releases most easily.

Heat the rest of the oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Cook the red pepper, baby marrow and spring onions for 4 to 5 minutes, until soft and any liquid has cooked away, which stops the cups going watery.
Add the spinach and stir for 1 minute, until just wilted. Spread the vegetables on a plate to cool for 5 minutes.
Divide the vegetables and cherry tomatoes between the 12 holes.
Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper in a jug until no streaks of white remain, then pour over the vegetables, filling each hole about three-quarters full.
Sprinkle over the cheddar and bake for 20 to 22 minutes, until puffed, golden at the edges and set in the centre; a knife pushed into the middle should come out clean.
Leave in the tin for 5 minutes, when they will sink a little, then run a knife around each one and lift it out. Serve three each, warm or cold.
prepNote: Keeps 4 days in the fridge or 2 months frozen; reheat in the microwave for 30 to 40 seconds, or eat cold.
